question.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 15 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}a & 5 \\ b & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $D={P}^{-1}AP,$ find the value of  $\frac{a}{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$

So, the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=-2.$ 

Now, we simply need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{1}=-2.$ Computing $A-(-2)I,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-2)I & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 15 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 15 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 15 & 0 \\ -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3}{5}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 15 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{3}{1}=3.$
